gen-dafont-nordic-gf-cascadia-mono: Nordic looks ancient and powerful, with tightly closed letters spaced far apart like brush dabs. Cascadia Mono takes over below with open, compact letters, giving the ancient heading a modern counterpart.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-julius-sans-one: Ancient and tightly shut, Nordic spaces its letters like far-apart brush dabs. Julius Sans One then runs on with wide gaps between letters and open curves, so a long block of it feels spacious and light.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega draws every letter as if with a single nib. Next to Nordic, which is closed and powerful, the body keeps a visible gap in every c, so pages of it read smoothly.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-lexend-peta: A monoweight stroke throughout gives Nordic its ancient, powerful and tightly closed look. And Lexend Peta, a sans-serif with wide-mouthed curves and a large x-height, lets paragraphs run on in an approachable voice.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-lexend-tera: Nordic is ancient and powerful, its letters closed tight and spaced like far-apart brush dabs, all in a monoweight stroke. Lexend Tera, a sans-serif, opens up wherever Nordic closes in.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-lexend-zetta: Powerful and ancient, Nordic closes its letters tight and spaces them like far-apart brush dabs. Lexend Zetta takes over with widely tracked, tall-bodied small letters, moving the page from closed shapes to open ones.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-montserrat-alternat: Ancient, tightly shut, Nordic hits hard. Montserrat Alternates, with a c as open as a bent paperclip, is the contemporary foil to all that closed, ancient power.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads compact and modern, its capitals blending into lowercase. Nulshock, technical and bold with stretched tracking and a steady outline, looks best given extra size over it.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-julius-sans-one: Technical and bold, Nulshock stretches its tracking wide and keeps a steady, unshaded outline on every letter. Julius Sans One then drifts across the page, light and spaced out.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-lexend-exa: Nulshock brings technical, bold lettering with stretched tracking and a steady, unshaded outline. Lexend Exa fills in with constant-thickness strokes and wide, distinct curves, and that outline-versus-solid gap is the whole appeal.
